nodes.description: Active iteration state computing next term of Taylor series

nodes.description: Multiply accumulated numerator by input numerator, divide by (i * denominator)

nodes.description: Check if accumulated numerator power has become zero (series converged)

ambiguities.text: No explicit bounds checking or overflow handling is documented for arithmetic operations.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume underlying type system (Uint, U32, U256) provides implicit bounds. Arithmetic relies on Python's arbitrary precision integers at the spec level.

ambiguities.text: le_uint32_sequence_to_bytes 'may preserve leading zeroes in most significant byte without trimming' - behavior is unclear.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume function always produces fixed-length output (4 bytes per U32) regardless of leading zeros. Caller is responsible for trimming if needed.

ambiguities.text: taylor_exponential loop termination condition only specifies 'while accumulated numerator remains positive' without maximum iteration bounds.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume series always converges for valid inputs due to factorial denominator growth. No explicit iteration limit is needed.

implicit_assumptions.description: Integer division behavior is consistent across all Ethereum client implementations (floor division).
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Different rounding modes could cause gas calculation discrepancies and consensus failures.

implicit_assumptions.description: Attackers cannot cause infinite loops in taylor_exponential by providing malicious inputs.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Denial of service through gas calculation that never terminates, blocking block production.

implicit_assumptions.description: Primality check using trial division is sufficient for the use cases (Ethash DAG parameters).
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: If non-prime values slip through, it could affect Ethash security properties, though impact is likely minimal.

implicit_assumptions.description: Little-endian byte ordering is consistently applied across all platforms and implementations.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Endianness mismatch would corrupt cryptographic operations and cause consensus failures.
